cards.text: Malachi, a prophet, has a word from the LORD for Judah, a people who've been breaking faith with God and with each other. He says it plain: "You have wearied the LORD with your words" and they fire right back, asking how. Ever tell somebody they're wearing you out and they answer "How?" like the question isn't the answer?

cards.question: The people ask how they've wearied the LORD with their words. What's one thing they've been saying?

answers.text: Evildoers are good in His sight
The prophets don't speak for Him

cards.text: Their other line is "Where is the God of justice?" I bet it's like me pressing my face on the oven door every ten seconds yelling WHERE ARE MY COOKIES.

cards.question: Then the LORD of Hosts speaks up. What does He say He will send?
The messenger the LORD sends will ___ the way before Him.

cards.text: Then the Lord they've been seeking will come to His temple, the one called the Messenger of the covenant. They've been looking for Him, and the LORD of Hosts says, see, He is coming.

cards.question: The Lord the people are seeking will come to His temple slowly, after a long wait.
The LORD of Hosts calls the Messenger of the covenant someone the people delight in.

cards.text: They wanted Him to show up, and He's coming, but then the hard question hits: "But who can endure the day of His coming?" Be careful what you ask for, friend, because sometimes it ANSWERS.

cards.question: Who can stand when the Lord appears? Why will it be so hard?

answers.text: He'll be like a refiner's fire
He'll come with a great army
He'll shake the earth and sky

cards.question: The Lord will be like a refiner's fire and like a launderer's soap. What do fire and soap have in common here?

answers.text: They both are kept in the temple
They both get used up fast

cards.text: Then the prophet says He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver. SIT, friend, like He pulled up a chair for this one.

cards.question: The Lord sits like a refiner of silver. Who will He purify and refine like gold and silver?
After the Lord refines the sons of Levi, the tribe set apart to serve the LORD, they stop bringing offerings to Him.
Once the refining is done, the offerings of ___ and ___ will please the LORD, just like in days gone by.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts says, "Then I will draw near to you for judgment." And He names who He'll stand against, and believe me, friend, this is NOT a list you want your name on.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts says He'll be a slow witness against these people and take His time.
The LORD names who He'll be a witness against. Which of these people is on His list?

answers.text: Those who cheat workers of their wages
Those who skip the yearly feasts
Those who eat food that is unclean

cards.question: The LORD says the people on His list have this in common: they do not ___ Him.

findings.problem: The card says Judah has been breaking faith with God and with each other. That comes from outside the passage (Malachi 2:10-11) and has no reference. The card cites only Malachi 2:17.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke says the people's "How?" is itself the answer to how they've wearied the LORD. In the text, the answer is what they've been saying in 2:17, which card 2 asks about. The comparison changes the action and muddies the fact right before the question.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "Heavy rain" is a different kind of thing from the other two answers, which are both people ("His messenger" and "A new king").

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "block" and "forget" aren't believable for a messenger sent ahead to deal with the way. "Forget the way before Him" doesn't make sense, so the right answer is obvious.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card is a flat retelling with nothing of Papa Dorin's voice. It also says the same thing twice ("they've been seeking" and "They've been looking for Him").

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The statement joins "slowly" to "after a long wait." The text says "suddenly" but says nothing about how long the wait is before He comes. A baker could argue "after a long wait" is true, so marking the statement False is open to dispute.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The punchline "sometimes it ANSWERS" doesn't hold together. It's unclear what "it" is or what answering means. The familiar idea is "you might get it," and the twist reads as a "huh?"

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The card asks two questions: "Who can stand when the Lord appears?" and "Why will it be so hard?" The answers only reply to the second one, so the first question reads as the thing being asked.

rule.text: A choice card is one question and its answers.

findings.problem: Malachi 3:3 says the sons of Levi will present offerings "in righteousness." That is the point of the verse, but no card tells it or asks about it. The question only checks whether they stop bringing offerings.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The sons of Levi are described as "the tribe set apart to serve the LORD." That comes from outside the passage and has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: In the two-blank card, a baker who puts "Jerusalem" in blank 1 and "Judah" in blank 2 would be marked wrong, even though the meaning is the same.
findings.question: When the two right words in a two-blank card can be swapped without changing the meaning, should either order count as right, or should the card be rewritten so only one order works?

findings.problem: The card says the LORD names who He'll "stand against." The text says He will be "a swift witness against" them.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: No card tells the list in Malachi 3:5: sorcerers, adulterers, perjurers, oppressors of the widowed and fatherless, those who defraud laborers, and those who deny justice to the foreigner. Card 18 asks about only one item, so the baker leaves without the rest.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card says everyone on the list "has this in common: they do not fear Him." In the BSB, "but do not fear Me" is attached to the last group: "those who defraud laborers of their wages and deny justice to the foreigner but do not fear Me." Whether it covers the whole list is left open by the text.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
